key_insight: A trust-limited Gaussian-process surrogate can accelerate NEB calculations for small-polaron hopping while preserving reliable barriers through targeted first-principles checks.
engineering_relevance: This workflow reduces the cost and convergence difficulty of DFT+U transition-path calculations in strongly localized electronic systems, enabling more practical defect- and ion-transport modeling.
method: Joint energy-force Gaussian process surrogate with a Matérn kernel
Trust-region limits on atom displacements plus active-atom RMS/max displacement triggers for DFT resampling
Independent full-band DFT verification, including a local GP for repeated central-image sampling
evidence_signal: Three independently verified 96-atom runs produced nearly identical barriers of 0.1645, 0.1637, and 0.1640 eV, and a 324-atom run gave 0.1302 eV with a final maximum projected NEB force of 0.0346 eV/Å.
watch_item: Barrier values remain sensitive to supercell size and charge-localization behavior, so surrogate extrapolation must be tightly controlled and always verified with DFT.
paper_title: Trust-Limited Machine-Learning-Accelerated Nudged Elastic Band Calculations for Small-Polaron Hopping in Rutile TiO2
